title: kbjob.py submit queues one job per clone, operation and subject, and a second submit returns the live job
goal: python3 _tools/kbjob.py [--store PATH] submit OP [SUBJECT] [--by claude-<8 hex>] [--option KEY=VALUE]... queues a job and prints one JSON object {job, state, deduped, seq, follow}: the key job/JB-<8 chars> holds {job, op, subject, host, clone, operator, by, options, state, attempt, submitted_ts}, moved none to queued by ST-hojylkmb's table; OP is one of the closed table kj_ops.OPS (land with the options wait_merge and trailer, done with commit and trailer, stage-back with check, self_reviewed and trailer, sync-push, check with --name one of backlog-check, tests-full, tests-changed), a backlog id is the SUBJECT of the first three and sync-push and check take none; an unknown operation (publish, answer), a subject that is no item of the clone, an option outside the operation's list or a --by that is no claude-<8 hex> exits 2 naming what is allowed; a second submit of the same clone, operation and subject (options aside) while the job is queued, running, waiting-lock, waiting-merge or lost returns the same job with deduped true, also when four submits race (one job), and after a terminal state a submit makes a new job with attempt raised by one; kj_store.submit(root, op, subject, by, options=None, store=None) returns that object and kj_store.status(root, job, since=0, store=None) returns {job, state, exit, step, log, events, last}, the one interface the MCP server calls

gates.question: How does submit make racing submits meet one winner: the item notes say jobkey/<hash> is written with put at the revision read, but the job record must carry its fields and coord's transition from none only creates {state: queued}
options: One BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction reads the triple key and the live job, then writes the key and a new stateless record; coord.job_transition then moves none to queued
put the triple key at the revision read, then put the record, then move it
gates.recommendation: One BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction reads the triple key and the live job, then writes the key and a new stateless record; coord.job_transition then moves none to queued
gates.reason: no orphan record and no key pointing at a job that was never written when a loser retries or the winner dies
gates.answer: One BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction reads the triple key and the live job, then writes the key and a new stateless record; coord.job_transition then moves none to queued

gates.question: What do the goal's undefined fields hold: status's log, submit's follow, and the record's clone and by
options: log is the end of job-logs/<job id>.log beside the store, follow is the coord.py wait command for the job's next move, clone is the main checkout shared by its worktrees, by is null when --by is not given
log is a path, follow is a hint text, clone is the working tree's path, by is required
gates.recommendation: log is the end of job-logs/<job id>.log beside the store, follow is the coord.py wait command for the job's next move, clone is the main checkout shared by its worktrees, by is null when --by is not given
gates.reason: the MCP caller needs text, the shell caller a runnable command, and one job per clone must hold from every worktree
gates.answer: log is the path of the job's output file, kb-jobs/<job id>/output.log under the git common directory (ST-rmv67pks's check opens it with os.path.exists, and the plan keeps output there), or null before the job ran; follow is the command line python3 _tools/kbjob.py follow <job id> (ST-5h2kx2ri's command); clone is the main checkout shared by its worktrees, so one job per clone holds from every worktree; by is null when --by is not given

gates.question: What forms may the options take, and is a name required for the check operation
options: flags take true, false, 1 or 0, wait_merge is 0 to 86400 seconds, trailer is one line of Key: value, self_reviewed is a doc path, trailer and self_reviewed repeat as lists, check requires its name
every option is free text and check defaults to the first name
gates.recommendation: flags take true, false, 1 or 0, wait_merge is 0 to 86400 seconds, trailer is one line of Key: value, self_reviewed is a doc path, trailer and self_reviewed repeat as lists, check requires its name
gates.reason: the executor builds argv from only validated text, so no value can pass for a flag

notes: Interface the paired MCP planner (plan/mcp-write) names: kj_store.submit(root, op, subject, by, options=None, store=None) -> {job, state, deduped, seq, follow} and kj_store.status(root, job, since=0, store=None) -> {job, state, exit, step, log, events, last}; job states queued, running, waiting-lock, waiting-merge, succeeded, failed, refused, cancelled, lost (terminal: succeeded, failed, refused, cancelled). Choices: module names kbjob.py with kj_* behind it, not ops*, so the query log's ops rows and backlog.py ops stay one meaning; the job id is random (kbid style) and idempotence is a coord key jobkey/<sha256 of clone path, op, subject> holding the live job id, written with put at the revision read, so racing submits meet one winner (coord.py:455 put, BEGIN IMMEDIATE at coord.py:274); a closed operation table is the authority rule: publish, answer and any operator-only command are no operation, and the executor runs only argv the table builds (the CLI's own gates and refusals then apply unchanged). by is claude-<8 hex>, never a full session id (memory claim-by-no-session-guid). No test is added: code.md allows tests only for critical parts and the suite sits at its ceiling; the planted checks above run the tool. Evidence measured 2026-11-08 from kb/_querylog/ops, real items 2026-10-02..2026-11-08: land.end ok median 103 s for content (p90 628 s, n=1701) and 430 s for code (n=133); orchestrator sessions held 285 foreground coord waits of 30 s or more, median 212 s, 20.8 h of 104.7 h file wall (20%).
